sources.cite: AWS. Lambda Developer Guide: Error handling for asynchronous invocation
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: 'If the function returns an error, by default Lambda attempts to run it two more times, with a one-minute wait between the first two attempts, and two minutes between the second and third attempts'; throttling (429) and system errors (500-series) are retried 'for up to 6 hours by default'; 'When an event expires or fails all processing attempts, Lambda discards it' unless a dead-letter queue or on-failure destination keeps it.

sources.cite: AWS. Lambda Developer Guide: Capturing records of asynchronous invocations (dead-letter queues)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: a DLQ (SQS standard queue or SNS standard topic) 'is used when an event fails all processing attempts'; Lambda sends 'the event to the dead-letter queue as-is', with RequestID, ErrorCode and ErrorMessage ('The first 1 KB of the error message') attributes; 'To reprocess events in a dead-letter queue, you can set it as an event source for your Lambda function. Alternatively, you can manually retrieve the events.'

sources.cite: AWS. CodeDeploy User Guide: Deployment configurations (AWS Lambda compute platform)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes 'Shifts 10 percent of traffic in the first increment. The remaining 90 percent is deployed five minutes later'; LambdaAllAtOnce 'Shifts all traffic to the updated Lambda functions at once'.

sources.cite: AWS. SAM Developer Guide: Deploying serverless applications gradually
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: with DeploymentPreference, 'if your pre-traffic or post-traffic tests fail, or if a CloudWatch alarm is triggered, CodeDeploy rolls back your deployment'; Alarms 'automatically roll back your deployment'; AutoPublishAlias publishes a new version and points the alias at it.

sources.cite: AWS. Amazon SQS API Reference: SetQueueAttributes
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: MessageRetentionPeriod 'from 60 (1 minute) to 1,209,600 (14 days). Default: 345,600 (4 days)'. The scenario's DLQ was created with 2 days.

sources.cite: AWS. IAM User Guide: Security best practices in IAM
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: AWS managed policies 'might not grant least-privilege permissions for your specific use cases'; reduce permissions further with customer managed policies specific to the use case.

brief.situation: Monday 14:20. You deployed version 42 of send-receipt, the Lambda function that emails order receipts, with AWS SAM in us-east-2 (Ohio). At 14:02 CloudFormation reported UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE: the canary was rolled back. The alias is back on version 41, and the dead-letter queue has events in it.
handover: The order service invokes send-receipt asynchronously, about 400 events a minute. Version 42 adds a new receipt template read from Parameter Store.
The SAM template deploys with Canary10Percent5Minutes and an alarm on the alias's Errors metric.
The DLQ is an SQS queue created with a 2-day retention period. Product wants version 42's template live today.
howItWorks: Learner-paced: nothing moves until you act. Read the output and logs, fix, redeploy, then run the next days.
The board shows which version serves and how it deploys; the meters show the DLQ and lost receipts.
Before you run the next days you are asked what failed and how you fixed it. The debrief scores what you did.

retryQ.title: Before the DLQ
retryQ.context: Each of these events failed with a function error. How many times did Lambda run it before sending it to the DLQ?

choices.label: Three times: the first try and two retries, about 1 and 2 minutes apart
choices.feedback: Right. For a function error on an asynchronous invocation, Lambda retries twice by default, then discards the event or sends it to the DLQ or an on-failure destination.

choices.label: Over and over for up to 6 hours
choices.feedback: No. The 6-hour retry window applies to throttling and system errors. A function error gets two retries by default.

plan.question: Before you run the next days: what made the deployment fail, how did you find it, and how did you fix it without losing receipts or the safety net?

parts.label: The cause, from the logs
parts.criteria: Traces the rollback from the stack events (alarm stopped CodeDeploy) to the function's own logs: AccessDeniedException on ssm:GetParameter for the new parameter; notes the failed events went to the DLQ after two retries.
parts.modelAnswer: The stack only says an alarm stopped the deployment. CodeDeploy shows the alias Errors alarm fired on the 10% canary, and the function's logs show why: the execution role cannot call ssm:GetParameter on the new template parameter. Those events failed three times and went to the DLQ.

parts.label: The fix and the recovery
parts.criteria: Grants ssm:GetParameter on the one parameter only; keeps the canary and its alarm; redeploys; redrives the DLQ through a working version before the 2-day retention expires; never purges it.
parts.modelAnswer: Add read access to that one parameter in the template, keep Canary10Percent5Minutes with its alarm, and redeploy. Then redrive the DLQ through the live alias so every receipt goes out, well inside the 2-day retention.

expertPath.text: Stack events: an alarm stopped CodeDeploy. CodeDeploy: the canary's 10% raised errors. Logs Insights on version 42: AccessDeniedException on ssm:GetParameter. The DLQ: 120 receipts, 2-day retention.
Grant ssm:GetParameter on the one parameter in the SAM template; keep the canary and alarm; sam deploy.
Version 43 passes its canary. Redrive the DLQ through the live alias. The trade-off: five more minutes per release for a canary that catches the next mistake on 10% of traffic.

broken.headline: A broken release reached every customer
broken.body: The canary and its alarm limited the first failure to 10% of traffic for three minutes. Redeploying without the fix and without that safety net sent every receipt into the same AccessDeniedException.

fixed.headline: Fixed from the logs, nothing lost
fixed.body: You followed the failure from the stack to CodeDeploy to the function's logs, fixed it with the narrowest permission, kept the canary and recovered every receipt from the DLQ. That is the expert path.

partly.headline: Shipped, by a rougher route
partly.body: Check whether you read the logs before changing things, whether the permission is limited to the one parameter, whether the canary kept its alarm, and whether the DLQ was redriven before it expired.

time_up.headline: No decision
time_up.body: The release waits and the DLQ ages.

scoring.modelReasoning: CloudFormation reports the symptom (an alarm stopped the CodeDeploy deployment), CodeDeploy says which alarm and when, and only the function's own logs say why: version 42's role cannot call ssm:GetParameter on its new parameter. Failed asynchronous events are retried twice and then sent to the DLQ, so the receipts are not lost yet, but the queue's 2-day retention is a deadline. Fix the cause with a permission on that one parameter, keep the canary and its alarm that limited the damage, redeploy, then redrive the DLQ through the working alias. Removing the alarm or shipping all at once trades a safe rollback for a full outage.
